Subject: Thanks for the call — next steps and test plan

Hi Sam —

Thanks for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery: NimbusHealth wants to validate parity vs your current hyperscaler provider for key features that matter to your product team — specifically function/tool calling, structured JSON outputs (schema enforcement + validation), and streaming for long-form generation. You also called out predictable tail latency and cost per token as gating factors for production.

Proposed next steps (short):
- We’ll run three focused tests (see details below).
- You’ll send a small set of representative prompts and a sample payload (if possible) so our SEs can run deterministic comparisons.
- We’ll share a test harness and a results template so you can reproduce locally.
- Schedule a 30-min sync at the end of the week to review results and procurement asks.

Attachments: sample_payloads.csv — please confirm this is representative (format: user_id, prompt, expected_function_response).

Initial test overview we propose:
1) Function calling correctness: verify that structured function calls map 100% to expected fields and edge cases (missing args, extra args, nested objects).
2) Structured outputs: enforce JSON schemas and run automated validators to check for extraneous/missing keys, types, and null handling.
3) Streaming behavior: 10k-token context test to ensure chunked streaming with stable connection and predictable per-chunk latencies.

We’ll compare Redwood vs your current provider (you mentioned Bedrock + Anthropic for some workloads) along these axes: correctness, latency (p95/p99), cost per token, and developer ergonomics (hooks for webhooks/function integrations, SDKs).

I’ll loop in Dev (SE) to propose the exact harness steps and provide the shell script and results template. Can we tentatively set the results review for Friday 2026-07-24 10:00 PT?

Thanks —
Marissa

Great — thanks for the payloads, Sam. High-level answers to your clarifying questions, plus the test plan we’ll run and what to expect from results: 

Function calling: Redwood supports function/tool calling with schema enforcement. We do automatic best-effort mapping, but for strict correctness we recommend using our function signature enforcement mode (we’ll show toggle in the harness) so functions only fire when shape+types match exactly. For webhooks: Redwood can call your webhook endpoint directly or emit structured events you can poll — whichever fits your topology. For parity vs Bedrock: bedrock has good auto-mapping; our enforcement mode reduces false positives/incorrect calls at the cost of stricter matching (safer for clinical workflows).

Structured outputs: Our runtime supports server-side schema validation and returns a "validation" object alongside generated JSON when you enable the feature. Tests will assert schema pass/fail counts and list diffs for mismatched fields.

Streaming: Redwood provides chunked streaming over HTTP (server-sent events / chunked transfer) and gRPC streaming for dedicated setups. For the test we’ll run a simulated client and capture per-chunk latency and jitter. We’ll also include a streaming trace to show how partial tokens are emitted.

Recommended test cases (we’ll run each on Redwood and on Bedrock/Anthropic as you have configured):
- TC1: Function calling — 50 prompts including malformed args, nested objects, and optional fields omitted.
- TC2: Schema enforcement — 100 prompts, validate returned JSON vs schema, measure pass/fail and error types.
- TC3: Streaming long context — 5 prompts with ~8–12k token context; measure p50/p95/p99 emit times and per-chunk sizes.
- TC4: Throughput smoke — batch 100 concurrent short prompts to measure tail latencies and error rates.

Links:
- Streaming docs: https://docs.redwood.com/streaming
- Function calling: https://docs.redwood.com/function-calling
- Test harness repo (read-only): https://github.com/redwood-inference/acme-test-harness

We’ll attach the harness script and results template in the next message. If procurement needs SOC 2, we’ll send our report and SOW.

—Marissa

Subject: Test harness + running steps (ACME/Nimbus tests)

Hi team —

Attaching a small test harness and results template: acme-redwood-test-harness.sh and results-template.csv. Quick runbook: 
1) Fork the repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/acme-test-harness (read-only)
2) Drop sample_payloads.csv into /inputs and run: ./acme-redwood-test-harness.sh --provider redwood --inputs inputs/sample_payloads.csv --out results/redwood-results.csv
3) Repeat with --provider bedrock (requires your Bedrock creds configured locally)
4) Harness will produce per-case JSON with fields: case_id, expected_schema_match (bool), function_call_fired (bool), p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms. Dump to results-template.csv.

A few notes: the script will run function-calling in enforcement mode by default; to emulate looser auto-mapping set --enforcement=off. For streaming we provide a --stream flag that drives a local SSE client and captures chunk timings.

Attachments in this message: acme-redwood-test-harness.sh (script), results-template.csv (CSV) — please run in a sandboxed environment; nothing accesses PHI.

Ping me if you want a live session where I run tests from our dedicated rig and share a screenshare.

—Dev (SE)
